title: Build a Financial Research Assistant with Cohere AI on AWS
gist: Cohere lays out a reference RAG architecture for financial filings on AWS: Cohere Embed/Rerank/Parse on SageMaker AI, OpenSearch Serverless as the vector index, and Anthropic Claude on Bedrock writing page-cited answers. The post is a design-tradeoff guide (Pro vs Fast tiers, 1,024-dim int8 vectors, selective parsing, Rerank Context Focus) that positions Cohere as the retrieval layer underneath a third-party generation model.

themes.theme: Cohere as retrieval layer, not answer model

insights.claim: Cohere's own reference architecture for a financial research assistant uses Cohere models only for embedding, reranking and parsing, while Anthropic Claude on Amazon Bedrock generates the final answers.
insights.speaker: @cohere
insights.so_what: Cohere is positioning its enterprise wedge as retrieval infrastructure that coexists with rival frontier LLMs rather than competing head-on for generation.
insights.quote: Anthropic Claude on Amazon Bedrock will be used to write the answers, with a citation for every claim.
insights.locator: In this post, we show how

insights.claim: The Cohere models in the reference design are distributed through AWS Marketplace and run as real-time Amazon SageMaker AI endpoints, with Amazon OpenSearch Serverless as the vector index and serverless AWS services for the app and ingestion pipeline.
insights.speaker: @cohere
insights.so_what: Hyperscaler marketplaces are a key go-to-market channel for Cohere, which deepens AWS dependence while widening enterprise reach.
insights.quote: The Cohere models run as real-time endpoints on Amazon SageMaker AI, deployed from AWS Marketplace; the vector index is Amazon OpenSearch Serverless
insights.locator: Under the hood there are two flows

insights.claim: Cohere argues that Rerank can improve keyword-based retrieval such as BM25 too, enabling Parse plus Rerank workflows with no embeddings at all.
insights.speaker: @cohere
insights.so_what: Rerank is pitched as a drop-in upgrade to legacy search stacks, broadening its addressable market beyond vector-DB adopters.
insights.quote: Rerank is not limited to vector search. It can also improve results from keyword-based retrieval methods such as BM25, enabling workflows like Parse + Rerank without requiring embeddings.
insights.locator: Choosing a pipeline for your documents

themes.theme: Why financial filings break naive RAG

insights.claim: In financial filings such as 10-Ks the needed figure usually sits in a table, footnote or chart, and plain PDF-to-text conversion destroys table row/column relationships, scrambles multi-column order and drops charts.
insights.speaker: @cohere
insights.so_what: Document parsing and layout-aware retrieval, not the LLM, is the binding constraint for finance AI accuracy.
insights.quote: When a PDF is converted to plain text, tables lose their row and column relationships, multi-column pages can come out in the wrong order, and charts often disappear.
insights.locator: Why financial research is hard to automate

insights.claim: Cohere holds that an AI answer without a verifiable source page is not useful to an analyst, so a finance assistant must cite filing, page and evidence type for every claim.
insights.speaker: @cohere
insights.so_what: Citation and auditability are table stakes for selling AI into regulated finance workflows.
insights.quote: An unverifiable answer is not useful.
insights.locator: An unverifiable answer is not useful

insights.claim: In the design, Claude must answer only from the five retrieved pages, state plainly when they lack the answer, and cite each claim as [document page | kind], where kind is table, chart, text, footnote or figure.
insights.speaker: @cohere
insights.so_what: Typed citations are a concrete pattern for reducing hallucination risk and speeding human verification.
insights.quote: Claude is also told to answer only from those pages, to say so plainly when they do not contain the answer, and to cite every claim in the form [document page | kind]
insights.locator: Let the answer model read the page

insights.claim: The system searches on page text but sends Claude the page image alongside the text and tells it to trust the image when they disagree, recovering charts and table structure that text extraction lost.
insights.speaker: @cohere
insights.so_what: Hybrid text-for-search, image-for-answer pipelines trade higher token spend for exact figures, which favors multimodal model demand.
insights.quote: tells Claude to trust the image where the two disagree
insights.locator: Let the answer model read the page

themes.theme: Cost-latency engineering: Pro/Fast tiers and vector compression

insights.claim: Embed Pro and Embed Fast share one embedding space, so pages can be indexed once with the higher-quality Pro model while live questions are embedded with the cheaper, faster Fast model without rebuilding the index.
insights.speaker: @cohere
insights.so_what: Asymmetric index/query model tiering is a pricing lever that lets Cohere upsell quality at indexing while keeping per-query costs low.
insights.quote: Embed Pro and Embed Fast share one embedding space, which means a question embedded with Fast can be compared directly with pages embedded with Pro.
insights.locator: Index with Embed Pro, query with Embed Fast

insights.claim: A 1,024-dimension int8 vector takes 1 KB versus 8 KB for a 2,048-dimension float32 vector, an 8x reduction, or roughly 1 GB versus 8 GB of raw vector data per million pages.
insights.speaker: @cohere
insights.so_what: Matryoshka and quantized embeddings compress vector storage sharply, a headwind to per-GB vector database revenue.
insights.quote: A 1,024-dimension int8 vector takes 1 KB of raw storage, compared to 8 KB for a 2,048-dimension float32 vector—an 8x reduction.
insights.locator: Storage

insights.claim: Cohere Embed offers six output sizes from 256 to 2,048 dimensions in float, int8 or binary, using Matryoshka representations in which the first dimensions carry the most meaning; binary is 32 times smaller than float32.
insights.speaker: @cohere
insights.so_what: Configurable dimensionality lets very large archives trade accuracy for cost without switching vendors.
insights.quote: Use 512, 256 or binary vectors for very large archives where cost dominates; binary is 32 times smaller than float32.
insights.locator: When to change it

insights.claim: Changing embedding size or format later requires re-embedding every page, so the choice locks in early and the query side must always match the index.
insights.speaker: @cohere
insights.so_what: Embedding choices create switching costs that make the index a sticky, vendor-locking asset.
insights.quote: Changing it later means embedding every page again, so it is worth settling early.
insights.locator: Whatever you choose, the query side

insights.claim: For pilots or bursty teams, idle GPU hours on always-billing real-time SageMaker endpoints are the largest cost, so the deployment has a single switch that removes all model endpoints while keeping data and index.
insights.speaker: @cohere
insights.so_what: Dedicated-endpoint economics are a real adoption friction for self-hosted model deployments versus per-token APIs.
insights.quote: For a pilot, or a team that works in bursts, idle GPU hours are the largest cost.
insights.locator: Make the expensive parts easy to switch off

insights.claim: Cohere routes only low-text and table-heavy pages to its GPU-billed Parse endpoint and caches the output so each page is parsed once, because clean digital pages already have usable text.
insights.speaker: @cohere
insights.so_what: Selective routing keeps document-AI costs proportional to document messiness rather than volume.
insights.quote: It is a GPU endpoint you pay for by the hour, and a clean digital page already has usable text, so we use it selectively.
insights.locator: Parse only the pages that need it

themes.theme: Rerank Pro and Context Focus token savings

insights.claim: Cohere chose Rerank Pro over Rerank Fast for financial research despite added query latency, arguing a wrong page costs more than a slower answer; vector search returns 30 candidates and Rerank selects five.
insights.speaker: @cohere
insights.so_what: In high-stakes verticals buyers pay for accuracy over speed, supporting premium-tier pricing.
insights.quote: because in financial research a wrong page costs more than a slower answer
insights.locator: Make Rerank an optional stage

insights.claim: Rerank Pro reads up to 32K tokens of question and page together, supports more than 100 languages and handles semi-structured content such as tables and JSON.
insights.speaker: @cohere
insights.so_what: Long-context, multilingual cross-encoders are Cohere's differentiated retrieval product spec.
insights.quote: Rerank Pro reads up to 32K tokens of question and page together, works across more than 100 languages, and handles semi-structured content such as tables and JSON.
insights.locator: Make Rerank an optional stage

insights.claim: Rerank 5 returns a calibrated 0-1 relevance score per page, so a fixed cut-off means the same thing across questions and can be used to tell users no page matches instead of answering from weak evidence.
insights.speaker: @cohere
insights.so_what: Calibrated relevance gives enterprises a mechanism to abstain, a key control for regulated use cases.
insights.quote: Rerank 5 also returns a calibrated relevance score between 0 and 1 for each page, so the same cut-off means the same thing from one question to the next.
insights.locator: When should you turn it on?

insights.claim: Cohere's internal evaluations claim Context Focus retains the vast majority of answer accuracy while cutting input tokens to the answer model by 50-75%.
insights.speaker: @cohere
insights.so_what: If it holds, Cohere's reranker reduces spend on the downstream frontier LLM, making Cohere a cost-saver alongside rather than rival to Claude-type models.
insights.quote: Cohere's internal evaluations show that Context Focus retains the vast majority of answer accuracy even when reducing input tokens by 50–75%
insights.locator: The tradeoff is context

insights.claim: Context Focus is weaker on structured content like tables and forms, whose relationships span sections, and full page content is generally better for broad tasks such as summarizing a page.
insights.speaker: @cohere
insights.so_what: Passage-level compression has limits precisely on the tabular data where finance answers live, so image context remains necessary.
insights.quote: Structured content, such as tables and forms, can be more challenging to split into meaningful chunks because important relationships may span multiple sections.
insights.locator: The tradeoff is context

insights.claim: Cohere advises leaving Rerank off when the right page usually lands at or near the top of vector search results, and adding it when the right page appears lower or questions are long and specific.
insights.speaker: @cohere
insights.so_what: Reranking is framed as an optional, measurable add-on, so its revenue depends on demonstrable lift per customer corpus.
insights.quote: If it is usually at or near the top, leave Rerank off and keep answers fast.
insights.locator: When should you turn it on?

insights.claim: Cohere Embed supports more than 100 languages and a 128K-token context window, so a French question can retrieve English Bank of America pages directly, removing a translation step and its mistranslation risk.
insights.speaker: @cohere
insights.so_what: Multilingual retrieval is a selling point for cross-border research teams and sovereign/non-English markets.
insights.quote: Embed supports more than 100 languages and a 128K-token context window.
insights.locator: One embedding space for every language

insights.claim: The demo runs on 928 pages of fiscal 2024 annual reports from Bank of America, Morgan Stanley and Wells Fargo drawn from the finance subset of the ViDoRe V3 benchmark, with sample questions in six languages.
insights.speaker: @cohere
insights.so_what: The showcase is a small benchmark corpus, not evidence of production-scale deployment at these banks.
insights.quote: It runs on three public annual reports (Bank of America, Morgan Stanley and Wells Fargo, fiscal 2024; 928 pages) from the finance subset of the ViDoRe V3 benchmark
insights.locator: Scope of the demo

insights.claim: The demo substitutes Rerank Fast for Rerank Pro because Rerank Pro needs larger GPUs and may face capacity constraints, and uses one ml.g5.xlarge instance per model in us-east-1.
insights.speaker: @cohere
insights.so_what: GPU availability and cost still shape which model tier customers can practically deploy.
insights.quote: Rerank Fast runs on smaller GPU instances, avoiding the higher GPU requirements and potential capacity constraints of Rerank Pro.
insights.locator: Rerank Fast instead of Rerank Pro

insights.claim: Cohere cautions that public benchmarks describe model behavior only on the benchmark's pages, not on a customer's own filings or scans, so every pipeline must be tested on in-house documents.
insights.speaker: @cohere
insights.so_what: Benchmark leadership is a weak proxy for enterprise retrieval wins; proof-of-concept results drive vendor selection.
insights.quote: A public benchmark tells you how a model behaves on that benchmark's pages, not on your filings, scans or company specific style guides.
insights.locator: Whatever you choose, test it

insights.claim: Cohere positions the same page-image-plus-text pipeline for insurance, legal, manufacturing and energy, public sector and life sciences documents wherever answers sit in tables, forms and layouts.
insights.speaker: @cohere
insights.so_what: Document-heavy regulated verticals are Cohere's targeted expansion market for retrieval products.
insights.quote: The pipeline is not specific to banks.
insights.locator: Beyond financial filings
